memory_update.text: KLAC should remain the reference benchmark for semiconductor process-control exposure, but not the main underfollowed alpha target due to mega-cap size and high investor attention.
CAMT is a high-priority discovery-lane candidate because it is US-listed, mid-cap, and explicitly tied to HBM, hybrid bonding, and advanced-packaging inspection/metrology.
ONTO is above the preferred $300M-$10B range but remains relevant because its process-control and advanced-packaging exposure is unusually direct.
PDFS should be tracked as a software/data yield-management candidate; current AI/HBM exposure needs stronger proof before upgrading from inference to fact.

Need a follow-up pass for other US-listed second-order vendors around process-control subsystems, probe cards, test sockets, equipment components, motion control, specialty optics, and outsourced calibration/inspection services.

node: Inspection, metrology, yield management, and process-control tools for advanced nodes, HBM, packaging, and PCBs
summary: Layer 1B expanded the US-listed universe around the process-control chokepoint. KLA remains the obvious reference leader for wafer, reticle, packaging, and PCB process control. The more underfollowed lane is concentrated in smaller or mid-sized public vendors with advanced-packaging/HBM inspection, metrology, and yield-data exposure: Camtek, Onto Innovation, and PDF Solutions. These names map to the hypothesis that AI-driven chip complexity, HBM, chiplets, hybrid bonding, and advanced packaging raise the economic value of defect detection, metrology, and yield analytics across multiple semiconductor winners rather than a single AI-chip design.
